scheme_name: Establishment of Entrepreneur for Breed Development in Small Ruminant Sector (Sheep and Goat Farming)
description:
The Establishment of Entrepreneur for Breed Development in Small Ruminant Sector scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2014. 

This initiative is aimed at enhancing the productivity and profitability of small ruminants such as sheep and goats. 

The scheme is part of the broader National Livestock Mission which was introduced in 2014. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to promote entrepreneurship in the small ruminant sector. 

It aims to increase the availability of quality breeding stock to improve the genetic potential of sheep and goats. 

The scheme also seeks to enhance the income of farmers engaged in sheep and goat farming. 

The target is to establish at least 1,000 entrepreneurs in the small ruminant sector across various states in India. 

The scheme focuses on providing financial assistance to entrepreneurs for setting up breeding units. 

Under this scheme, the government provides a subsidy of 25% to 50% of the total project cost. 

The exact percentage of subsidy depends on the location of the project. 

For instance, projects in hilly and scheduled areas receive a higher subsidy of 50%. 

The financial assistance can cover costs related to infrastructure development, purchase of breeding stock, and operational expenses. 

The maximum project cost eligible for subsidy is set at INR 30 lakhs. 

This means that an entrepreneur in a scheduled area can receive a subsidy of up to INR 15 lakhs. 

The scheme also includes provisions for training and capacity building of entrepreneurs. 

Training programs are conducted to enhance the skills of farmers in breeding, management, and health care of small ruminants. 

The eligibility criteria for applicants under this scheme include being a resident of India. 

Applicants must be at least 18 years old and should have a minimum educational qualification of 10th standard. 

Additionally, applicants should have experience or knowledge in animal husbandry. 

The application process involves several steps. 

First, interested applicants must submit a project proposal to the nearest Animal Husbandry Department. 

The proposal should include details such as the location, type of breeding stock, and infrastructure plans. 

Required documents include identity proof, address proof, educational certificates, and any previous experience in animal husbandry. 

Once the proposal is submitted, it is reviewed by a committee at the district level. 

If approved, the applicant is notified and can proceed with the implementation of the project. 

The disbursement of the subsidy is linked to the completion of project milestones. 

Entrepreneurs must submit progress reports to receive subsequent installments of the subsidy. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The contact details for the Department can be found on their official website. 

The scheme has been instrumental in improving the livelihoods of many farmers across the country. 

As of 2023, over 800 entrepreneurs have been established under this scheme. 

The initiative has contributed to a significant increase in the population of improved breeds of sheep and goats. 

This has led to enhanced meat and wool production in various states. 

The scheme also promotes sustainable farming practices among small ruminant farmers. 

It encourages the use of scientific breeding techniques and better management practices. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 200 crores for the implementation of this scheme over a five-year period. 

This budget is aimed at supporting various activities including training, infrastructure development, and financial assistance. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of women’s participation in the small ruminant sector. 

Special provisions are made to encourage women entrepreneurs to take up sheep and goat farming. 

The government aims to empower women by providing them with equal access to resources and training. 

The scheme has also been linked with the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana. 

This linkage provides additional financial support to farmers engaged in small ruminant farming. 

The government has also introduced various awareness programs to promote the benefits of this scheme. 

These programs aim to educate farmers about the advantages of improved breeds and better management practices. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries who have reported increased incomes. 

Many entrepreneurs have successfully expanded their operations and created employment opportunities. 

The government continues to monitor the progress of the scheme through regular evaluations. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the implementation process. 

The scheme aligns with the government’s vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

It also contributes to the overall goal of enhancing food security in the country. 

The establishment of entrepreneurs in the small ruminant sector is seen as a vital step towards achieving sustainable agriculture. 

The scheme has also been instrumental in promoting rural development. 

By enhancing the productivity of small ruminants, it helps in improving the economic conditions of rural households. 

The government encourages partnerships with NGOs and private sector players to enhance the reach of the scheme. 

These partnerships aim to provide additional resources and expertise to entrepreneurs. 

The scheme is expected to evolve further with the introduction of new technologies and practices in the livestock sector. 

Overall, the Establishment of Entrepreneur for Breed Development in Small Ruminant Sector scheme represents a significant effort by the Indian government to boost the small ruminant sector. 

It aims to create a sustainable and profitable environment for farmers engaged in sheep and goat farming. 

The scheme reflects the government's commitment to improving the livelihoods of rural communities through targeted interventions. 

As the scheme progresses, it is anticipated that more farmers will benefit from the opportunities it provides. 

The focus on entrepreneurship and breed development is expected to have a lasting impact on the small ruminant sector in India.
